The '''1979–80 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|78th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|49th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
During summer changes came to the bench, [[Real Zaragoza]]'s Yugoslavian head coach [[Vujadin Boškov]] signed in to replace [[Luis Molowny]] as new trainer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1979/06/05/deportes/297381619_850215.html|title=Boskov will Replace Molowny as Real Madrid Coach|work=El País|date=4 June 1979|accessdate=2 July 2020|author=José Damián González|language=Spanish}}</ref> After the departure of Danish Forward [[Henning Jensen]] to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax Amsterdam]], the club seek to reinforce the left side, rumours included several players such as [[René van de Kerkhof]] from [[PSV Eindhoven]] and [[Rüdiger Abramczik]] from [[Schalke 04]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1979/08/28/deportes/304639211_850215.html|date=27 August 1979|accessdate=27 August 2021|title=Boskov pleaded not to compare him to Miljanic|publisher=elpais.com|language=es|author=Alfredo Relaño}}</ref> however the manager favoured the arrival of [[Laurie Cunningham]] who became the first British player to play for the club, the forward was transferred in from [[West Bromwich Albion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-37924448|title=The match that pitted white players against black players|date=17 November 2016|accessdate=18 November 2016|author=Adrian Chiles|work=BBC News}}</ref> Defender [[Goyo Benito]] received La Laureada (The Laureate) from President [[Luis de Carlos]] due to his outstanding compromise and playing for the club being only one of two players with that distinction.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2007/09/20/mas_futbol/1190269622_850215.html|title=Benito and Pirri The Only Two Players with La Laureada|publisher=as.com|date=20 September 2007|accessdate=2 July 2020}}</ref> Other two players reinforced "The Madrid of Los García"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/opinion/2019/10/18/5da99d9122601d1b308b4623.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=28 October 2019|title=Real Madrid: The Madrid of Los García|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> such as Perez García from [[Real Madrid Castilla]] and [[Antonio García Navajas]] from [[Burgos CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/10/17/5da8a87a22601dcd0e8b45dd.html|date=17 October 2019|work=Marca|location=Spain|accessdate=2 July 2020|title=Former Real Madrid defender Angel Passed Away}}</ref> 

In the [[1979–80 European Cup|European Cup]], the team reached the [[1979–80 European Cup#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] where it was eliminated by Western German side [[Hamburg SV]]. Despite winning 2–0 in Madrid, the squad plummeted in the second leg of the series to lose 1–5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1979/06/05/deportes/297381619_850215.html|title=Madrid played a disgraceful Match|date=23 April 1980|accessdate=2 July 2020|author=Alfredo Relaño|language=Spanish|work=El País}}</ref> Meanwhile, in the [[1979–80 Copa del Rey]] the squad advanced to the [[1980 Copa del Rey Final|final]] and won the trophy against its reserve team [[Real Madrid Castilla]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-40-anos-final-copera-irrepetible-20200604132308.html|publisher=europapress.es|title=An Unrepeatable Final|language=Spanish|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=4 June 2020}}</ref> 6–1 in front of 65,000 spectators at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thesefootballtimes.co/2016/05/19/when-real-madrid-castilla-reached-the-copa-del-rey-final-and-played-in-europe/ |title=When Real Madrid Castilla reached the Copa del Rey final and played in Europe |work=[[These Football Times]] |date=19 May 2016 |accessdate=2 July 2020 |last=McTear |first=Euan }}</ref>

The club clinched its 20th League title which became its third [[Three-peat#Spain|three-peat]] ever<ref>After winning 1961–63 and 1967–69.</ref> by just one single point above runners-up emerging [[Real Sociedad]]<ref>Real Sociedad won head-to-head matches 4–0, 2–2.</ref> after the then-undefeated in last 32 league matches basque side lost its game on round 33 against [[Sevilla CF|Sevilla]] thanks to 2 goals of [[Daniel Bertoni]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20120210/real-sociedad/bertoni-el-hombre-que-le-quito-la-liga-a-la-real-en-1980-se-la-pedi-a-gaztelu_54251703395.html|title=Bertoni the man who took La Liga away from Real Sociedad|publisher=mundodeportivo.com|date=10 February 2012|accessdate=2 November 2020}}</ref> Added to its [[1980 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey]] trophy, the team won its third "[[Double (association football)#Spain|Double]]" ever and their fifth league title in the last six seasons.
